findings.message: An invalid `-n` value exits with status 1 and omits the command usage line. The documented conventions require invalid option arguments to report a usage error and exit 2, so callers cannot distinguish this from a file read failure.

`$@` is unquoted, so filenames containing spaces are split and wildcard characters can expand before `lk_check_files` checks them. This can reject valid filenames or check different paths than the command will read; preserve the arguments with `"$@"`.

parsed.summary: The new option handling violates the documented usage-error convention, and the file check breaks filenames containing whitespace or glob characters.

pull_request.title: number: add -n START to begin numbering at START
pull_request.body:
Adds `-n START` to `linekit number`, so a numbered excerpt can keep the line numbers of the file it was cut from:

    sed -n 120,140p f | linekit number -n 120

The command table in README.md is updated.
